extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Administrators, and NIH extramural staff
extracted.subtask_description: High-level NIH Office of Extramural Research guidance describing how applications are peer reviewed (initial SRG review and second-level advisory council review), the objectives of review (evaluate and rate scientific/technical merit), and specific policy areas (human/animal subjects, inclusion, data safety, oversight).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and rating of scientific and technical merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the initial peer review is to evaluate and rate the scientific and technical merit of the proposed research or research training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial peer review groups composed of scientists from the extramural research community perform an evaluation and rating of applications' scientific and technical merit. This is the stated primary purpose guiding SRG deliberations and scoring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial peer review conducted in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review of applications submitted to the NIH takes place in multiple steps; the initial step takes place in Scientific Review Groups (SRGs) that are managed by Scientific Review Administrators (SRAs) located in the Institutes and Centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRGs are the organizational units that manage primary scientific review. SRAs located in ICs administer SRGs. The CSR manages SRGs for investigator-initiated applications; IC review branches manage SRGs for special solicitations such as RFAs and unique programs. Proper assignment to the appropriate SRG is implied as part of correct review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate application referral & management by CSR and IC review branches
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Scientific Review (CSR) manages SRGs that evaluate investigator-initiated applications; Review Branches of awarding institutes and centers manage SRGs for applications submitted in response to special solicitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application referral to the correct NIH component (CSR vs. IC review branch) determines which SRG reviews the application; guidance and further information about application referral and peer review is available on the CSR website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review by NIH National Advisory Councils
rubrics_metrics.description: The second level of peer review is carried out by NIH National Advisory Councils composed of scientists from the extramural research community and public representatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These Councils provide advice and ensure that NIH receives input from a cross-section of the U.S. population during deliberation and funding decisions. Council rosters and meeting schedules are maintained and used in this process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protection and inclusion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must consider protection of human subjects and inclusion issues (women, minorities, children) when evaluating applications involving human subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references specific guidance documents: 'NIH Instructions to Reviewers for Evaluating Research Involving Human Subjects in Grant and Cooperative Agreement Applications' (April 5, 2002), 'Peer Review Decision Trees for Human Subject Protection and Inclusion Issues', and topic pages such as 'Protection of Humans', 'Women in Clinical Research', 'Minorities in Clinical Research', and 'Children in Human Subjects Research'. Reviewers should follow these documents and decision trees when assessing human-subjects aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for human and animal subjects research
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must meet NIH requirements for human and animal subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An 'Important Notice to Applicants: Requirements for Human and Animal Subjects Research' (April 27, 2001) is cited. Reviewers and applicants should ensure compliance with the policies described in that notice when preparing and evaluating proposals involving human or animal subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in clinical trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical trials require appropriate data and safety monitoring plans, which reviewers should evaluate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'Data and Safety Monitoring Plans in Clinical Trials' as a topic for reviewers; reviewers are expected to assess whether monitoring plans are adequate for the proposed trials per NIH policy and guidance documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit statements of review criteria for rating applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH has announced explicit statements of review criteria used to rate grant applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page references 'Rating of Grant Applications - NIH Announces New Explicit Statements of Review Criteria' (June 1997). While the specific criteria are not enumerated on this page, it signals that reviewers should use NIH's explicit review criteria (as promulgated in that and related documents) when assigning ratings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer Review Oversight to ensure reviewer expertise and process quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Peer Review Oversight Group (PROG) advises and makes recommendations on development and implementation of policies for monitoring, coordinating, and evaluating peer review to ensure processes keep pace with research advances and reviewer expertise matches scientific needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PROG's function includes oversight of peer review policies and practices. The PROG roster and meeting minutes are maintained; applicants and reviewers can consult PROG outputs to understand oversight priorities. This implies a criterion that peer review processes should be regularly monitored and updated and that reviewer expertise must be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of public representatives/participants in scientific peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH incorporates public representatives/participants into scientific peer review processes to ensure broad perspectives are represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page lists 'Inclusion of Public Representatives/Participants in Scientific Peer Review' as a specific workgroup/issue, implying that inclusion of public or lay members is an explicit policy consideration when composing review panels or advisory bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of SRG and Special Emphasis Panel membership (rosters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rosters of membership for NIH Scientific Review Groups, standing review committees, and Special Emphasis Panels are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making reviewer rosters available supports transparency about who is performing reviews. Applicants and stakeholders can consult rosters to understand panel composition; SRAs/ICs maintain these rosters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing regulatory burdens through workgroups
rubrics_metrics.description: Workgroups are established to address regulatory burdens related to peer review and related policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page notes 'Workgroups Established to Address Regulatory Burdens', indicating that evaluating and reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens is a policy objective that can affect how reviews and requirements are structured and enforced.
